newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares end higher after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares end higher after U.S. data.

text.p: 1545 GMT - Swiss shares ended moderately higher on Tuesday after fresh U.S. economic data dampened interest rate worries and gave the market a boost in the afternoon session, dealers said.
They said the market was likely to continue its moderate rise until Friday's expiry of options and futures because some investors had to cover open positions.
* Broad SPI up 6.10 points to record close of 2,555.41.
* Blue-chip SMI up 8.1 points to 3,983.6 record close.
Nestle, up 14 francs to 1,466, led the actives list. Novartis fell one to 1,560 and UBS added two for 1,156.

Dealers said there was new buying interest from abroad. NatWest Securities said it put three Swiss shares on its list of 15 European stocks expected to outperform during 1997. It also picked Switzerland as a favourite market.
The three shares listed were Clariant, up 16 to 612, Credit Suisse Group, steady at 134.75, and Roche, which rose five to 10,740.
Banks, recently neglected, drew some new interest. SBC added 2.25 francs to 250,50.
Second-tier shares saw SEZ Holding higher. EMS Chemie rose on several buy recommendations.
Soffex activity centred on Nestle and UBS options. Nestle is expected to release its 1996 sales figures on January 21.
136,159 options were traded at a call-put-ratio of 1.3 to 1. Bank Leu's volatility index eased 61 basis points to 17.68 percent.
SMI futures saw further rollover-transactions ahead of Friday's expiry. 11,662 contracts were traded. January SMI rose seven points to 3,984 while the February contract added 9.5 to 3,993 points.
